title: How the Python SDK retries: budget, statuses, waits, re-authentication

prose.text: These are claims about the Python SDK's OneAPI request executor, shared by every product. The Go SDK's retries are in [[shared.sdk-go.retries]]; each product's own rate limits and wait headers are in its rate-limits subject, for example [[zia.api.rate-limits]] and [[zcc.api.rate-limits]].

prose.label: Expired tokens.
prose.text: {{reauth-on-401}} A legacy client has no OAuth handler to re-authenticate with: [[zdx.sdk-python.legacy-client:no-reauth]].

max-retries.statement: The executor reads `client.rateLimit.maxRetries` from the configuration with a default of 2, and rejects a negative value.

quotes: raise ValueError(f"Invalid max retries: {self._max_retries}. Must be 0 or greater.")

max-retry-seconds.statement: A rateLimit maxRetrySeconds setting caps the wait: a computed backoff above it raises RetryTooLong instead of sleeping.

quotes: f"Retry wait time {backoff} seconds exceeds configured maxRetrySeconds {max_retry_seconds}."

wait-from-headers.statement: The retry wait comes from Retry-After plus one second, or else from the rate-limit reset header plus one second; with neither header the request is not retried and an error is returned.

retryable-statuses.statement: The Python executor's retryable-status helper documents 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504 as retryable, but its code tests only 429, 503 and 504, so a 500 or 502 is not retried by it.

quotes: return status is not None and status in ( # HTTPStatus.REQUEST_TIMEOUT, # HTTPStatus.CONFLICT, # HTTPStatus.PRECONDITION_FAILED, HTTPStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, HTTPStatus.GATEWAY_TIMEOUT, )

method-not-consulted.statement: The branch that retries the retryable statuses (`TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT`) is decided by `attempts < max_retries` and `is_retryable_status(response.status_code)`, and `is_retryable_status` takes only the status; the request method is not consulted.

quotes: # Handle "retryable" statuses such as 429, 503, etc. if attempts < max_retries and self.is_retryable_status(response.status_code):

return status is not None and status in ( # HTTPStatus.REQUEST_TIMEOUT, # HTTPStatus.CONFLICT, # HTTPStatus.PRECONDITION_FAILED, HTTPStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, HTTPStatus.GATEWAY_TIMEOUT, )

reauth-on-401.statement: On a 401 the executor clears the OAuth token, fetches a new one and retries while attempts remain; otherwise it returns a token-refresh-exhausted error.

quotes: Got 401 response; clearing token and re-authenticating.
401 Unauthorized - token refresh attempts exhausted or OAuth not available.
evidence.after: # Check for 401 -> Trigger re-auth if we still have retries left

checks.do: Whether a write that timed out with a 503 or 504 was retried and so possibly applied twice, since the retry does not look at the method.
